action: Place probe in the subcostal window. Orient the probe slightly oblique to the patient's body rather than perfectly sagittal. Manipulate the angle to 'open up' the organ completely.
interpretation: Target the gallbladder. Acknowledge that a sagittal view of the gallbladder usually requires an oblique probe angle relative to the body axis.

action: Identify the structure and sweep through the entire organ.
Maintain position in the subcostal window. Prepare to change planes.
interpretation: Transitioning to obtain a transverse image of the gallbladder.

action: Visually assess probe physical orientation. Rotate the probe exactly 90 degrees.
interpretation: Align probe geometry to be perfectly set up for the transverse view.
Confirm visualization of the transverse plane.

action: Rotate the probe 90 degrees in the opposite direction.
interpretation: Return to and confirm the sagittal plane.
